 Jake Dickert reveals to FOX Sports contract extension in works at Wake Forest
 Thomas Goldkamp 2h 0 Share Share 
 Wake Forest coach Jake Dickert has become one of the hottest names on the coaching carousel, even before it begins to spin at full speed. According to a report from FOX Sports , he is working on an extension with the Demon Deacons but it has not yet been finalized.
 Until it is, other programs will undoubtedly be doing their due diligence on the second-year Wake Forest coach, who previously engineered a turnaround at Washington State . But Dickert isn’t overly focused on that.
 [ $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] 
 He opened up on the state of contract extension talks with Wake Forest in a lengthy piece by Ben Portnoy . In short, he likes his position. FOX Sports notes “extension discussions are ongoing, though school officials declined to specify further” and exact details are expected to “be finalized in the coming weeks.”
 “They know exactly where I sit,” Jake Dickert said of the Demon Deacons brass. “I want to be here. I want to be here with these coaches and these players. To me, they’re the priority, not me. Once that’s done, we’re good.”
 With NIL playing such a big part in roster construction these days, how competitive programs can be is often a direct corollary to how attractive they can be to coaches. Dickert said that Wake Forest is in the bottom third of the ACC in spending.
 Can Wake Forest put together a package — not just for Jake Dickert but for his program — that is compelling enough to keep him? The FOX Sports article dives into what’s being done on that front and it’s illuminating.
 Still, the fact remains that Dickert remains on multiple hot boards: he’s on On3’s Pete Nakos’ at Florida State and Bryan Fischer of Sports Illustrated’s at Baylor , among others.
 Dickert is blunt, though. He’s perfectly willing to stay, if the right conditions are met. He reiterated that to FOX Sports a couple times in the Portnoy piece.
 “We didn’t come here to leave,” Dickert said. “I say that really honestly and truthfully. … There’s this lane that we can be really successful in. I just say we can’t be sputtering in this lane. We can’t be walking in this lane. We have to be sprinting in this lane, and I believe we can do that — and I believe with the expanded playoffs, there can be a lot of opportunity here.”
 Up next is a significant challenge when it comes to reaching that last goal. Wake Forest sits at No. 13 in the College Football Playoff rankings. It’s within striking distance.
 Can Jake Dickert and company keep on course with a road trip to SMU this weekend? Win that one and the whole picture begins to open up. In any case, for now, Wake Forest seems to stand a good shot at retaining its head coach. There’s certainly mutual interest in a lasting partnership.
